text:
A: Hiya! Can you hear me alright? Yusuf.
B: Yes, fine. I'm Carys.
A: Carys, nice. Are them walking boots behind you? By the door?
B: They are, yes. I'm in the hills most weekends. Moel Famau, usually.
A: Proper outdoorsy, then. I'm more gym, if I'm honest. Indoors, with air con.
B: That's fair. Less mud.
A: Way less mud. So what do you do?
B: Civil engineer. Flood risk and drainage, for local authorities mostly.
A: No way, so this is actually relevant to me. I'm an exec assistant at a commercial property consultancy in Birmingham, and every other board meeting I'm minuting, somebody's going on about a flood risk assessment holding up a site.
B: That'll be people like me holding it up, then.
A: Ha, so it's your fault! What actually goes in one of them?
B: Erm, you look at where the water comes from, river, surface water, sometimes groundwater, and what happens when you put buildings and car parks on top of it. Then you have to show you're not just pushing the problem onto the next street. Which developers sometimes try.
A: Mate, I believe that. Our lot would definitely try that.
B: Most do. It's usually fine once you show them the model.
A: I'm actually trying to move into business development, so I'm meant to be learning all this. I've mentioned it to one of my directors.
B: Good. Learn the boring bits properly, though. People can tell quite quickly if you're bluffing.
A: Yeah. Yeah, that's fair. Noted.
B: Sorry, that came out like a lecture. I mentor graduates, it's a habit.
A: No, no, it's good advice. Did you do the puzzle at the start? I reckon I got them all.
B: All of them?
A: Most. Most of them. Okay, I'm being generous to myself.
B: I thought you might be.
A: You've rumbled me. That's three people today. Holidays, anything nice?
B: Pembrokeshire this summer, walking. I did the Dolomites once with a university friend, that was the best one.
A: The mountains in Italy? That's the kind of place I'd go for the photos. I always want somewhere new, me, I never go back anywhere twice.
B: I'd go back. It took us four days to stop being lost.
A: Four days lost in Italy. That's a good story, that, you should tell it more.
B: I'd probably tell it worse than you would.
